decision.rationale: At100M the best-loss model is Sparse+Ngram, but its mixed/code advantage over Sparse is only0.006509/0.005529 nats (about0.65% mixed perplexity improvement), while its stored capacity is larger and cumulative step cost about4.77% above Sparse. All72 individual primary arithmetic task attempts fail. The key surviving architecture question is whether current memory adds a reproducible incremental benefit over the same grouped sparse backbone. Replicate this pair, not all three. Continue both fresh seed1337 runs cumulatively through20M/50M/70M/100M with the same100M LR horizon;100M is chosen because the small incremental gap and curve shape cannot be settled by a50M-only endpoint. Document bootstrap does not measure training-seed uncertainty.
decision.pair_difference: Current Ngram alone; same grouped backbone/active-compute policy.
decision.no_dense_replication: Dense remains the seed42 baseline; this second-seed comparison resolves the extra-memory survivor decision and does not replicate the Dense gap.
